upgradePolicyWhy: THIS FILE IS NEVER RELEASED BACKWARDS-COMPATIBLE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. webpieces validates it on startup, so when a key moves or is renamed the loader REJECTS the old shape and hands you an error naming the destination ('X moved to Y'). Apply that edit and re-run — the error IS the migration. Every reader of this file is an AI agent, so upgrades are seamless without webpieces shipping a compatibility layer for every old shape. Never add a fallback that accepts both shapes: two accepted shapes means two code paths forever, and an accepted shape is NEVER migrated, so the dead one lives here indefinitely. You cannot get stuck — editing this file is always allowed even while it is invalid, and `pnpm install` is always allowed (a validator lagging this file by a release is the most common failure; install first, do NOT start by deleting keys). `pnpm wp-install-ai-hooks --sync` performs the mechanical migrations. Any key ending in 'Why' is a rationale note like this one; unknown keys are rejected, so name notes '<key>Why'. Full policy: .webpieces/instruct-ai/webpieces.config-policy.md

pr-gate.buildCommandWhy: --base is the FORK POINT via $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD), NOT origin/main: basing on origin/main marks projects from other people's already-merged PRs as 'affected' (your branch still has their pre-merge versions), wasting rebuilds. The fork point scopes affected to only your branch's work. The $(...) resolves because the gate runs with shell:true.
pr-gate.buildCommand: pnpm nx affected --target=ci --base=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)
pr-gate.mergeModeWhy: NONE while the L2 guard changes are under human review — the repo owner asked for merge to be OFF so these PRs can be rejected rather than landing themselves. Stage 3 still repairs squash_merge_commit_title=PR_TITLE / squash_merge_commit_message=PR_BODY (SquashSettingsEnforcer), so a human clicking Merge on GitHub now writes the SAME bytes the tooling would have: the PR title plus the compact risk/flags body. That is what makes NONE safe here, and it is why the previous AUTO rationale (a UI merge would land raw branch commit messages) no longer holds. Flip back to AUTO to let wp-finish-upsert-pr land PRs again.
pr-gate.checklistsWhy: backwards-compat-reviewer enforces this repo's INVERTED compatibility policy: a changed webpieces surface must make the OLD spelling stop compiling, with the error naming the new one. It is required because every consumer of these surfaces is a coding agent, and an agent picks whatever typechecks — a @deprecated tag is not part of the type, so a soft landing freezes callers instead of migrating them (issue #589: an agent wrote the widest auth grant onto an admin contract and asserted the framework had no role support). Patterns are deliberately COARSE — every framework package, every API contract, and the config itself — because the reviewer makes the content-level judgment by reading the diff. error-output-reviewer enforces the ONE error contract across both rule engines: a failure is THROWN as a structured value (RuleFailError carrying Option[] cures, or InformAiError for plumbing) to the single top-level handler for the process, which renders it per audience. It is required over packages/** for the same reason — every consumer of this output is a coding agent, and a console.error in the middle of a validator cannot be rendered per audience, suppressed, or tested, and can print a cure that is unreachable because nothing type-checks a string literal against the code around it. A THIRD reviewer, experiment-lifecycle-reviewer, exists at .claude/agents/experiment-lifecycle-reviewer.md with its checklist at .claude/review/experiment-lifecycle.md and is NOT registered here yet — its entry lands in the follow-up PR. The reason is a bootstrap constraint, not a doubt about the reviewer: the Claude Code harness builds its agent registry when a session starts, so an agent file created during a session cannot be spawned in that same session, and a PR registering a brand-new REQUIRED reviewer would be refused by its own provenance check ("1 never ran") with no way to satisfy it. Landing the agent file first, then its checklists entry, is the same ordering this repo already uses for a rule and the config key that turns it on.
pr-gate.gatesWhy: warningColor (REQUIRED on every gate) = the dashboard color shown WHEN a gate's patterns match a changed file (green is implicit when nothing matches; warningColor is purely visual and never blocks the PR — only the build gate can). disabled:true gates are kept-in-file examples (JSON has no comments) other projects flip to false and tune; they are skipped on this repo.

commands.guardHintsWhy: The command strings the PR-lifecycle guards print in their fix hints. prCreationOrPush -> the push/PR-creation block, mergeInProgress -> the unvalidated-merge block. This is the ONLY place these strings live: the per-guard upsertPrCommand / mergeCompleteCommand fields were second spellings of these, they BEAT this section at the point of use, and they are now DELETED. Rename a gated command here and every guard message follows — which is true as of the 9->3 hookGuards collapse, and was not true before it.

excludePathsWhy: ONE glob list, honoured by every hook guard (Bash, Read and Write/Edit alike — see runner.ts filterByExcludedPaths). `repositories/**` is vendored foreign code. There is deliberately NO entry for `.webpieces/**`: the tooling's own gitignored state dir is skipped in CODE (isWebpiecesStateDir, consulted by filterByExcludedPaths ahead of this list and regardless of it), so a config entry would be a second and WEAKER spelling — `.webpieces/**` compiles to an anchored regex that misses the bare directory the predicate matches. The entry that used to sit here was the one-release-lag placeholder its own note scheduled for deletion; the release that ships isWebpiecesStateDir (0.4.675) is now pinned, so it is gone.

match-rules.name: no-fetch
match-rules.mainMessage: Raw HTTP (fetch/axios/XMLHttpRequest/…) bypasses contract-first development — the client and server stop sharing the same API contract/types. Generate a type-safe client from the contract instead:
options: PREFERRED: generate a client from the API you want to call — server-side, inject ClientHttpFactory from '@webpieces/http-client-node' and call factory.createRpcClient(SomeApi, new ClientConfig('some-svc')); in a browser, use ClientHttpBrowserFactory from '@webpieces/http-client-browser'. Then: await client.someMethod(req);
Reuse an existing API contract already defined in your repo (under libraries/apis/**) and generate its client the same way.

For a truly external service, create a NEW API contract (a decorated abstract class) AND a NEW implementation that calls fetch behind that contract, under an allowlisted dir (libraries/apis-external/**). The contract stays the shared surface; fetch is an impl detail.

match-rules.name: no-global-providesingleton-in-packages
match-rules.mainMessage: Framework code in packages/** must use @provideFrameworkSingleton (a SEPARATE DI registry) so a client's buildProviderModule() never scoops up webpieces framework classes. Plain @provideSingleton is for apps/client code only. (Turn ON once the repo consumes a @webpieces release whose DI-graph analyzer understands provideFrameworkSingleton.)
options: In a packages/** framework class, use @provideFrameworkSingleton() (self-bind) or @provideFrameworkSingletonAs(TOKEN) from @webpieces/core-context.
WebpiecesRouter loads buildFrameworkModule() + buildProviderModule(); any embeddable WebpiecesRouteCreator user must also load buildFrameworkModule() to resolve framework filters.
